syndrome that is seen with rapid correction (Rhoda et al, 2011).
Hypernatremia.  ​A serum sodium level greater than 145 mEq/L 
is classified as hypernatremia, and there are various types. 
Hypovolemic hypernatremia is caused by a loss of sodium and 
TBW when water losses exceed sodium losses. It is important to 
identify the cause of the fluid losses so that they can be corrected 
and prevented in the future. The treatment is to slowly replace 
fluid volume with a hypotonic fluid solution. Hypervolemic 
hypernatremia is caused by excessive intake of sodium resulting 
in higher sodium gain than water gains. The treatment is to 
restrict sodium (especially in intravenous fluids) and possibly 
the use of diuretics. Isovolemic hypernatremia is seen with 
disease states such as diabetes insipidus. Signs of hypernatremia 
include lethargy, thirst, hyperreflexia, seizures, coma, or death.
